name: streamed-vesting-hbar
description: On-chain vesting that unlocks itself with HIP-1215 scheduled contract calls and settles every claim in native HBAR through the SaucerSwap V2 router. No bot, no relayer, no cron.

instructions: +This template streams an HTS grant token to a beneficiary and pays out in native HBAR.
Unlocks are scheduled on chain with HIP-1215, so there is no bot or relayer to run.
+1. Fill in the operator credentials in .env, using values from the Hedera portal.
+2. Compile and run the contract suite:  {pm} run compile && {pm} test
The script prints the contract ID when it finishes.
+4. Copy the printed NEXT_PUBLIC_* lines into .env, then start the dashboard:
The grant token must have a SaucerSwap V2 pool against WHBAR at the fee tier you
configure. Hedera testnet defaults to SAUCE, which has one at the 0.30% tier.

HIP-1215 removes the bot
steps.text: At grant time the contract calls the Hedera Schedule Service (0x16b) once per release, asking it to call executeClaim at a future consensus second. When that second arrives the network performs the call. There is no off-chain component to keep running, and a release the network refuses is reported rather than reverted, so executeClaim stays permissionless and the stream still settles.

steps.label: The SaucerSwap swap is mandatory
steps.text: Every claim converts the vested grant token into WHBAR and unwraps it to native HBAR through the SaucerSwap V2 router. The beneficiary cannot end up holding the grant token, and the swap carries a quoted floor so a claim cannot fill below the agreed price. Removing the swap removes the product. That also means the grant token must have a live SaucerSwap V2 pool against WHBAR at the configured fee tier, or every claim reverts.

steps.label: Hedera gotchas this template already handles
steps.text: Hedera system contract calls never revert: they return an int64 ResponseCodeEnum ordinal where 22 is SUCCESS, so every one is checked as a value. The Schedule Service is 0x16b and HTS is 0x167, which are routinely misquoted for each other. The router pulls its input with transferFrom and exposes no ERC-20 approve, so the allowance is granted through HTS. And an HTS token cannot move to an unassociated account, so the deploy script associates the parties with the grant token first.

steps.label: All package.json scripts
steps.command: {pm} run compile | {pm} test | {pm} lint | {pm} build | {pm} run dev | {pm} run clean | {pm} run deploy:testnet | {pm} run deploy:mainnet
